I have certainly shocked people with a turn 3+ charge by Kabalites onto an objective, but it is always a last resort.  Hitting on 2s takes people by surprise, and I have seen people get nervous about it.  It's especially hilarious in Killteam, when Orks think that they are about to win and get smacked around by weedy gits with piercings.  


That said it's a LAST RESORT and better to arm those Trueborn with Blasters, arm the Archon with Blasters, and only charge after you have blastered the bajezus out of everything first.  And only if I can't just safely stay in a transport.
Wracks or Grots can have Liquifiers, as can Haemis.

6 liquifiers (4 grots, 2 haemis) would be 21 S3 auto hitting shots on average.  With the variable AP you're talking 10 Wyches or Gants, 7 Orks, or 4 MEqs when they charge.  That's more damage than a Tau Sept Firewarrior squad on overwatch with a Fireblade nearby.  And there is still a Raider to get through before you get to the meat inside.  That's pretty horrifying, actually.

Honestly I'd be happy enough if an aura ability worked on the OTHER units INSIDE the vehicle (and the vehicle itself.)  It would be nice to be able to drop my Blaster Archon in a Raider with BlasterBorns and let them reroll their ones.  And any ones from the Dissie on the Raider.  Or if you pack a Venom full of Slyth, getting to reroll the Ones on those Shardcarbines and the Splinter Cannons outside.  Otherwise the Aura negation thing is really just to balance us getting 6-10 ablative wounds on our GEqs and double their speed for our highly accurate shots.  Letting us use Auras too would be pretty rough.
Yeah, pink is really fun.  I tried using actual pink paint when I first started doing it on hair, but just doing white with a red wash looks fantastic.

"Embarked units cannot normally do anything or be affected in any

way whilst they are embarked. Unless specifically stated, abilities

that affect other units within a certain range have no effect whilst

the unit that has the ability is embarked." -Battle Primer pg 9  


The very act of being embarked makes auras not work.  Silly, but there we are.  Just giving you the RAW requested.

It's actually a 22.5% increase in damage to give them liquifiers against MEqs, assuming you move in, spray your target, then charge them. Against less resiliant armies it is far, far more deadly.  The Flesh Gauntlet has its mortal wound chance being used as well (even though it's not a huge increase, but it works better than the cleaver against Inv Save dependant units)  The issue of course is that it is also a \~31% increase in cost.  So if you are weighing percentages for cost/benefit, yeah, this could be an issue. But given that it gives you an overwatch option for anyone charging you, and certain units will now be deterred from attacking you, you are now looking at a place where the points disparity is worth considering and not dismissing outright.  Since the initial question was the matter of having auto hitting weapons and letting embarked units Overwatch against chargers against the transport, hopefully you will understand how that might be unbalanced.  This is, of course, to say nothing of a Trukk full of Burna Boyz.
There are literally dozens of us!

On this topic, if you do take a shardnet, you should not need more than one, due to how shardnets are worded.  Instead, take Hydra Gauntlets.  It is very easy to get to a 2+ to hit in combat, making the rerolls to hit from Flails not as useful as the rerolls to wound of the Gauntlets, which are good regardless of the enemy toughness.

That being said, after turn 3 Kabalites are surprisingly nasty in CC.  After 4+ turns of shooting, most armies are softened up to a point that a kabalite charge finishes them off.  Don't plan for it, don't pay for it (blast pistols and agonizers on Sybarites? Ugh, no!) but don't make it your last resort, either. Just let it exist in your brain as an option.

Except that "they" is an indefinite pronoun. You also used "they" to refer to Facists.  Therefore "they" in your statement "Then I guess they're both functioning and nessesary." could refer to "Facists," "Antifa," or both "Facists" and "Antifa" at once.  Based on the context, any of these are possible. One is more likely, but only if we assume you, the faceless speaker about whom we otherwise know nothing, has a particular viewpoint that you are trying to espouse.  We would require further context. Thus, your statement was confusing and required further clarification.    


It's not really your fault. It's English.  But the more you're aware of it, the better your arguments can be.
